kinds.name: Claude Code plugins and mods
kinds.title: Claude Code Plugins and Mods: Marketplaces, Hooks, Mods
kinds.meta: Claude Code plugins, mods, marketplaces, hooks and status lines: the official catalogs, the install commands and reviewed community repositories.
kinds.lead: A plugin is a folder of skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers that Claude Code installs as one unit. A mod is a plugin whose JavaScript or TypeScript handlers run inside Claude Code itself, so it can draw panes, add commands and guard tool calls.
intro: Plugins install from a marketplace with /plugin install name@marketplace, or from a repository with /plugin marketplace add owner/repo. Anthropic's own marketplace is added on the first interactive session; everything else is a catalog you add yourself.

Mods are the same package with one extra file: hooks/hooks.json names a modules entry, and the module exports a register function that subscribes to events such as tool calls, prompt submissions and interface draws. Claude Code 2.1.287 or later runs them. They are not sandboxed: a mod runs with your permissions, so read what it registers before you install it.

install.heading: How a plugin installs
install.text: Inside Claude Code, add a marketplace once, then install plugins from it. The same commands work from the shell as claude plugin marketplace add and claude plugin install. Validate a mod before installing it with claude plugin validate, which prints the hooks it registers and the calls it makes.

faq: What is the difference between a plugin and a mod?

A plugin is a folder of components that Claude Code installs as one unit: skills, agents, settings hooks, MCP servers and language servers. A mod is a plugin that also ships a hooks module, JavaScript or TypeScript code that runs inside Claude Code and can draw interface elements, add commands and change tool calls.
How do I install a Claude Code plugin?

Add its marketplace with /plugin marketplace add owner/repo, then run /plugin install name@marketplace. Anthropic's claude-plugins-official marketplace is already present on the first interactive session. From a shell, the same commands are claude plugin marketplace add and claude plugin install.
Are mods safe to install?

A mod runs with your permissions and is not sandboxed. Run claude plugin validate on the folder first: it prints the hooks the mod registers and the calls it makes. Prefer mods from publishers you know, and read the register module before enabling it.
Does the directory grade plugins and mods?

No. The Suede Skill Check scores skills from their SKILL.md folders. Plugins and mods are listed from their publisher's repository with a short description; they carry no score, no security result and no verification badge.

kinds.lead: Grok Build is xAI's open-source terminal coding agent. It reads AGENTS.md, skills, plugins, hooks and MCP servers, and installs plugins from a marketplace pinned to commits. Beside it sit the bots people build on the Grok API for Discord and other chat apps.
intro: Grok Build installs with one command and keeps skills in .grok/skills in a project or ~/.grok/skills for a user. Plugins use a .grok-plugin folder with a plugin.json manifest and the same components as other agent plugins: skills, commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers. The plugin marketplace is built into the terminal and every remote plugin is pinned to a commit.

Bots on the Grok API call the xAI Responses API with function calling, search and image generation. The repositories below are community projects unless marked official; read their setup notes and token handling before you run one.

faq: What is Grok Build?

Grok Build is xAI's terminal coding agent, published as open source under Apache-2.0. It reads AGENTS.md, Agent Skills, plugins, hooks and MCP servers, and installs plugins from a marketplace where every remote plugin is pinned to a commit.
Do skills from this directory work in Grok Build?

Yes. Grok Build reads skills from .grok/skills in a project and ~/.grok/skills for a user, and the skills CLI installs there with npx skills add owner/repo -a grok. Every skill page shows the command for its folder.
What is a Grok bot?

Two things share the name. Grok Bot is xAI's hosted product: a named bot with a persistent cloud computer, skills and routines, included with an X subscription. A Grok bot in a repository is a community program that calls the Grok API from a chat app such as Discord.
Does the directory grade these repositories?

No. They are listed from their publisher's repository with a short description. The Suede Skill Check scores skills only, and nothing on this page carries a score, a security result or a verification badge.

kinds.name: MCP servers
kinds.title: MCP Servers: Reference, Official and Featured Projects
kinds.meta: Model Context Protocol servers: the reference implementations, the official registry, popular official servers, and the MCP projects featured here.
kinds.lead: A Model Context Protocol server gives an agent access to a system it cannot reach on its own: a browser, a database, a billing API. A skill teaches the method; a server supplies the tools. The best setups pair the two.
intro: Claude Code reads servers from .mcp.json in a project or from a plugin's mcpServers entry; Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Goose and Grok Build have their own configuration files for the same servers. The official registry publishes a server.json for each listed server with a verified namespace.

A server holds credentials and acts on outside systems, so check what tools it exposes and what scopes its keys carry before you add it. The directory lists servers from their publisher's repository or official documentation and does not score or scan them.

faq: What is an MCP server?

A program that speaks the Model Context Protocol and exposes tools an agent can call, resources it can read and prompts it can use. It usually holds the credentials for an outside service, such as a database or a billing API.
Should I use a skill or an MCP server?

Use a skill when the agent has the access it needs and is missing the method. Use a server when the job needs data or actions the agent cannot reach with files and a shell. Many featured projects in this directory pair a server with the skills that know how to use it.
How do I add a server to Claude Code?
Run claude mcp add with the server's command or URL, or commit a .mcp.json file in the project. Plugins can also declare servers, so one install brings the skills and the tools together.
Are the servers here scanned or scored?

No. Servers are listed from their publisher's repository or official documentation with a short description. They carry no quality score, no security result and no verification badge from the directory.

kinds.name: Rules, instruction files and prompts
kinds.title: AGENTS.md, Cursor Rules, CLAUDE.md and Prompt Libraries
kinds.meta: Instruction files and prompts for coding agents: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md templates, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions, persona files and prompt libraries.
kinds.lead: Before an agent loads a skill it reads the instruction files in your repository: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions. These collections hold reviewed examples, templates and the standards that define the formats.
intro: AGENTS.md is a plain Markdown file at the repository root that most coding agents read, including Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and Claude Code when no CLAUDE.md is present. Cursor adds project rules in .cursor/rules as .mdc files with scoping frontmatter; Copilot reads .github/copilot-instructions.md and path-specific instruction files.

Persona files such as SOUL.md and prompt libraries such as Fabric's patterns are the same idea for assistants that live in chat apps: text the agent loads every session. None of these carry code, which makes them the easiest layer to review before you adopt them.

install.heading: How instruction files install
install.text: Copy the file into the place your agent reads. Most of them need no tooling: AGENTS.md goes at the repository root, Cursor rules into .cursor/rules, Copilot instructions into .github, CLAUDE.md beside your code. Plugins for Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI install with each product's own command.

faq: What is AGENTS.md?

A plain Markdown file at the repository root with instructions for coding agents, stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation. Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and Grok Build read it, and Claude Code reads it when the project has no CLAUDE.md.
Where do Cursor rules go?

Project rules live in .cursor/rules as .mdc files with description, globs and alwaysApply frontmatter. A plain .md file in that folder is ignored. Cursor also reads AGENTS.md at the root and in subfolders.
Do these files run code?

No. Instruction files, rules and prompts are text the agent reads. That makes them the easiest layer to review, but a file can still steer an agent toward risky actions, so read it before you adopt it.
Are these collections graded?
No. They are listed from their publisher's repository with a short description and carry no score, security result or verification badge. The Suede Skill Check applies to skills only.
